disease_label_per_paper: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state as the first manifestation of type 1 diabetes mellitus in an adolescent male
presentation_summary: 17-year-old boy presented to the emergency department with severe polydipsia and lethargy.
He had 7 days of anorexia and 3 days of polyuria and polydipsia, with weight loss from 55 kg to 44 kg over the prior month.
Admission vitals were temperature 37.0 degC, heart rate 96/min, respiratory rate 22/min, and blood pressure 118/70 mmHg.
Physical examination showed mild drowsiness with Glasgow Coma Scale score 13 and intact sensation and motor strength.

Initial laboratory data showed glucose 1456 mg/dL, serum osmolarity 359 mOsm/kg with effective osmolarity 323 mOsm/kg, BUN 67.9 mg/dL, creatinine 2.93 mg/dL, sodium 143 mmol/L, corrected sodium reported as 156.6 mmol/L in the text, venous pH 7.327, bicarbonate 16.4 mmol/L, base excess -7.65, potassium 5.7 mmol/L, chloride 94 mmol/L, urine glucose 3+, and urine ketones 1+.

risk_context.source_text_value: previously healthy with no personal or family history of diabetes; later diagnosed with type 1 diabetes
severe polydipsia, polyuria, anorexia, and weight loss over a month

observations.source_text_value: previously healthy; no history of endocrine disease including diabetes mellitus
weight decreased from 55 kg to 44 kg in the past month
serum osmolarity of 359 mOsm/kg (effective osmolarity, 323 mOsm/kg)
initial serum sodium level was 143 mmol/L
corrected sodium level of 156.6 mmol/L in narrative text
serum urea nitrogen level of 67.9 mg/dL
HHS criteria in the case allow small or absent ketonemia; no serum ketone value reported

course_observations.source_text_value: Table 2 corrected sodium 165 mEq/L at 20 hours

confirmatory_findings.finding: Paper diagnosis of HHS due to type 1 diabetes mellitus
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The patient was diagnosed with HHS due to T1DM

confirmatory_findings.finding: Anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody positivity supporting T1DM

actual_treatment: cautious fluid replacement for estimated 20% deficit over 72 hours
500 mL 0.9% normal saline bolus for 1 hour
intravenous insulin infusion initially 0.1 U/kg/hr then reduced to 0.025 U/kg/hr after HHS confirmation
mannitol for possible cerebral edema due to headache and drowsiness

outcome.source_text_value: After 34 hours of fluid administration, mental status became alert and headache subsided; serum glucose and corrected sodium gradually improved with no neurological complications observed.

quality_warnings: Type 1 diabetes classification and antibody testing are confirmatory/non-ranking; they are not part of the first-layer HHS disease name.
The text reports corrected sodium 156.6 mmol/L while the table lists initial corrected sodium 161 mEq/L; the narrative value is used for the rankable snapshot and the discrepancy is preserved here.
Small urine ketones and mild acidosis are kept as rankable presentation evidence rather than deleted; they represent HHS-DKA boundary context without forcing a combo label.
